rules.title: Berkeley ban on the sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or manage occupancy (BMC ch. 13.63)
rules.requirement:
Two acts are unlawful:
- Selling, licensing or otherwise providing to Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley (§ 13.63.030(A)).
- A landlord using such an algorithm when setting rents or occupancy levels for Berkeley units (§ 13.63.030(B)).

A coordinated pricing algorithm is any analytical or computational process that uses Competitor Data to calculate and recommend rent prices, fees, occupancy rates or other rental contract terms for future leases. The recommendation must be made in coordination between a Berkeley landlord and one or more of its competitors, including through a third-party vendor.

Competitor Data is non-public information less than 90 days old about another landlord's property, such as:
- actual rents;
- occupancy rates;
- lease start and end dates.

For landlord use, each month of violation and each unit is a separate violation.

Enforcement:
- The City Attorney may sue under subsection A or B for damages, injunctive relief, restitution of illegal profits and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation.
- An aggrieved tenant may sue under subsection B for injunctive relief, money damages and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation.
- The prevailing City Attorney or tenant is awarded reasonable attorney's fees and costs.
- Lease clauses limiting a tenant's fee recovery are unenforceable.

The chapter does not regulate the amount of rent. It does not bar software that helps landlords manage units generally or through public data.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each unit is a separate violation (landlord use); Competitor Data = non-public data less than 90 days old; mandatory attorney's fees to prevailing City Attorney or tenant

coverage.summary: Applies to vendors that sell, license or provide coordinated pricing algorithms to Berkeley landlords, and to landlords using them for any residential dwelling unit in Berkeley. No limits by unit count, building age or landlord size are stated.

rules.effective_date_note: The captured ordinance text has no effective-date clause and no final adoption date. rules.title: Berkeley tenant screening fee disclosure and ban on non-refundable fees for existing tenancies (BMC ch. 13.78)
rules.requirement:
Disclosure (BMC 13.78.010): an owner or agent who charges an applicant a fee to buy a consumer credit report and to validate, review or process an application must provide two statements before receiving the fee, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure:
- a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement;
- a statement of the maximum fee cap under Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b).

Existing tenants (BMC 13.78.016): an owner or agent may not charge an existing tenant a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy, in whole or in part. This includes fees tied to a roommate's departure or to a request to add or replace a roommate.

Scope (BMC 13.78.018): the chapter applies to all residential rental agreements despite contrary lease language, and conflicting lease provisions are unenforceable.
rules.key_value: Pre-payment disclosure of screening fee rights and the state fee cap; no non-refundable renewal or roommate fees for existing tenants. The dollar cap comes from state law (the Berkeley Rent Board lists $68.96 for 2026).

coverage.summary: Applies to owners of residential rental property in Berkeley and their agents, and to all residential rental agreements regardless of contrary lease language. It complements the state screening-fee cap in Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6.
coverage.other_conditions: The fee cap, receipt, credit-report copy and refund rules are state law (Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6) and are not part of this record.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance Annual General Adjustment (AGA) limit on rent increases (BMC § 13.76.110)
rules.requirement:
Landlords of fully covered units may raise the rent ceiling each year only by the Annual General Adjustment (AGA) set by the Rent Board.

Formula and cap:
- The AGA is 65% of the Bay Area CPI-U increase, a formula approved by voters in November 2004.
- Measure BB (November 2024) caps the AGA at 5%.
- Landlords with banked (unused) AGAs from earlier years may still raise rent above 5% to reach the rent ceiling.

2026 AGA (Regulation 1148, adopted Oct. 16, 2025):
- 1.0%, which is 65% of the 1.5% CPI increase for July 2024 to June 2025.
- It applies to the 2025 permanent rent ceilings no earlier than January 1, 2026.
- It may not adjust rents for tenancies that began on or after January 1, 2025 whose rents were set under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act.
- Regulation 1148 sets the qualifying conditions and the required tenant notice.

Other Measure BB changes:
- Rent ceiling increases for capital improvements may be petitioned only for completed improvements.
- For fully covered tenancies starting on or after Feb. 6, 2024, utilities must be included in base rent or separately metered in the tenant's name.
- Government-owned or -subsidized units registered as fully covered now have rent ceilings.
rules.key_value: 2026 AGA 1.0% (65% of 1.5% CPI), effective no earlier than Jan. 1, 2026; AGA capped at 5%, though banked AGAs may exceed 5% up to the rent ceiling

rules.effective_date_note: The documents give no effective date for the underlying ordinance or for Measure BB's 5% cap; Measure BB passed in the November 2024 election. rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.
rules.conflict_note:
Open question on the new-construction cutoff. Two official Rent Board documents disagree:
- The coverage guide (D009) treats units with a certificate of occupancy after June 1980 as partially covered, while it describes fully covered multifamily units as 'built before 1980'.
- The Measure BB page (D006) says 'certificate of occupancy issued after 1980'.
Coverage of units with a certificate of occupancy from roughly January to December 1980 is unresolved. The cutoff recorded here follows D009.
rules.review_note: State context: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12 exempts housing under stricter local rent control, so the AGA governs fully covered units. Partially covered units have no local rent control and may fall under the state cap, subject to its own exemptions (15-year rolling new construction, qualifying single-family homes and condos with notice). The ordinance text and Regulation 1148 are not captured, so conditions for taking the AGA and notice content are not shown. The organizer's mention of a 30-year exemption is not applicable; no such statute appears in the documents.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance just cause for eviction, notice requirements and owner move-in relocation (BMC ch. 13.76, as amended by Measure BB)
rules.requirement:
Tenants in fully or partially covered units may not be evicted without just cause.

Measure BB changes:
- Nonpayment eviction requires rental debt of at least one month of HUD Fair Market Rent for an equivalent unit (Oakland-Fremont metro).
- A tenant cannot be evicted for refusing to sign a substantially similar new fixed-term lease.
- Lease-breach evictions require a mutually agreed material term, substantial actual damage to the landlord, and unreasonable tenant behavior.
- The required notice to cease must specify the term and describe the violation and harm.

Notices and filings:
- Every termination notice must state that advice is available from the Rent Board and give its housing counseling phone number and website.
- Copies of termination notices, notices to quit and summons and complaints must be filed with the Rent Board within three business days of service.
- For tenancies starting on or after Dec. 20, 2024, landlords must give a Notice of Tenant Rights within 15 days and post it in any interior common area.

Owner move-in relocation:
- Owners must pay relocation assistance in an owner move-in eviction.
- The amounts are indexed to inflation and adjusted annually by the Rent Board (mandatory under Measure BB).
- From Jan. 1, 2026: $19,413 standard and $6,471 additional for qualifying households.

Coverage changes:
- Shared kitchen or bath units are exempt only if the landlord lived on the property before the tenancy began.
- Government-owned or -subsidized units are now fully or partially covered.
rules.key_value: Nonpayment eviction only if debt is at least 1 month of HUD FMR; filings with the Rent Board within 3 business days; tenant rights notice within 15 days; owner move-in relocation $19,413 standard + $6,471 for qualifying households (from Jan. 1, 2026; 1.5% CPI adjustment)
